lessonRef.title: Transfer, reflection, and publication: estimating and checking in everyday situations

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different setting than the problems below.

steps: The nearest multiples of 100 are 600 and 700.
647 is 47 away from 600 and 53 away from 700.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: You read a word problem and are not sure what it is asking. What should you do first?
choices: Skip the problem without trying it.
Guess an answer and move on to the next problem.
Restate the problem in your own words and identify what question is being asked.
Multiply every number in the problem together.

items.prompt: A problem has more numbers in it than you need. What should you do before solving?
choices: Decide which numbers the question actually needs before setting up the work.
Guess an answer and move on to the next problem.
Skip the problem without trying it.
Multiply every number in the problem together.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: You solved a problem, but the answer seems much too large for the situation. What should you do?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
